pr.title: coverage: Improve handling of function/closure spans
pr.description:
This is a combination of some loosely-related changes that touch the same code:

1. Make unexpansion of closure bodies more precise, by unexpanding back to the context of the closure declaration, instead of unexpanding all the way back to the top-level context. This preserves the way we handle async desugaring and closures containing a single bang-macro, while also giving better results for closures defined in macros.
2. Skip the normal span-refinement code when dealing with the trivial outer part of an async function.
3. Be more explicit about the fact that `fn_sig_span` has been extended to the start of the function body, and is not necessarily present.

---

@rustbot label +A-code-coverage
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Coverage instrumentation was computing closure body spans by unconditionally unexpanding to the outer macro call site, which lost the closure declaration context for closures declared inside macro expansions. The fix unexpands only to an ancestor in the same syntax context as the closure declaration, and separately hoists async-function span handling so the trivial desugared outer async body skips normal span refinement. `fn_sig_span` was also made optional because closures may have no usable signature span.
analysis.originalLogic: In `extract_hir_info`, `body_span` came from `get_body_span`, which did: `if tcx.is_closure_or_coroutine(def_id.to_def_id()) { body_span = body_span.source_callsite(); }` after `let mut body_span = hir_body.value.span;`. The old comment explained that for a closure whose body span was created by macro expansion or compiler desugaring, it tried to walk backwards to the pre-expansion call site or body. Separately, `mir_to_initial_sorted_coverage_spans` always seeded `initial_spans` with `vec![SpanFromMir::for_fn_sig(fn_sig_span)]`; for async functions it skipped body spans but then cleared spans only via `if initial_spans.len() == 1 { initial_spans.clear(); }`. `fn_sig_span` was non-optional, falling back with `.unwrap_or_else(|| body_span.shrink_to_lo())`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect span transformation replaced a closure body span with `body_span.source_callsite()`, i.e. it unexpanded all the way back to the top-level macro call context. For a closure declared inside a macro expansion, this collapses the body span to the outer expansion context instead of the closure declaration's own context. The corrected transformation uses `body_span = body_span.find_ancestor_in_same_ctxt(fn_decl_span).unwrap_or(body_span)`, unexpanding only to the closure declaration context. Separately, the old async handling ran normal span refinement over the unhelpful desugared outer async function spans; the correction hoists an early branch that keeps only the signature span when `hir_info.is_async_fn`.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-eligible Rust functions and closures whose HIR body spans arise from macro expansion or compiler desugaring. The key domain is closures declared inside `macro_rules!` expansions (especially where the closure body is a single bang-macro invocation), plus async closures/functions whose desugared outer body contains spans that are not user-meaningful. Ordinary top-level closures with directly written body spans are not the triggering case.
analysis.trigger: A closure is declared inside a macro expansion, or its body consists of a single bang-macro invocation, so its HIR body span has a different/synthetic context from the declaration. Also triggered when instrumenting an async function whose outer desugared wrapper spans would otherwise be refined into coverage mappings.
preconditions: The function or closure is eligible for coverage instrumentation and the InstrumentCoverage pass is running.
The closure's body span was created by macro expansion or compiler desugaring, so it is not already in the declaration's syntax context.
For the async branch, the HIR item is an async function whose body is the compiler-desugared wrapper around user code.
A usable signature span exists only if it shares the body's syntax context and filename and precedes the body; closures may have no such span.
pitfalls: Unconditionally calling `source_callsite()` unexpands too far, discarding the closure declaration's intermediate macro context and losing closure body instrumentation.
Use `find_ancestor_in_same_ctxt(fn_decl_span)` for closure bodies so nested macro/async desugaring is preserved rather than flattened to the outermost call site.
Do not run normal span refinement over the trivial desugared outer async function; hoist the async special case before refinement and keep only the signature span.
`fn_sig_span` must be optional: closures can have no function signature span, and a candidate signature span is only usable when it has the same context and filename as the body and precedes it.
When a body has spans but no usable signature span, add a fake span from `body_span.shrink_to_lo()` before refinement to avoid a gap; do not add the signature span when the body yielded no spans.
Coverage attributes on closures interact with enclosing functions; tests include `#[coverage(on/off)]` on both global and local closures.
analysis.testStrategy: Add/update `tests/coverage` fixtures with `.rs` input plus expected `.coverage` line counts and `.cov-map` mappings. Use `macro_in_closure.rs` with `static NO_BLOCK: fn() = || println!("hello");` and a block-bodied `WITH_BLOCK` closure to pin closure-body span unexpansion. Use `coverage_attr_closure.rs` to pin `#[coverage(on/off)]` on global and local closures. Update `closure_macro.rs` and `closure_macro_async.rs` so the closure declared inside `on_error!` is instrumented (replace the FIXME comment), and assert the closure's coverage map now contains multiple body mappings instead of a single whole-closure mapping. Do not claim execution; fixtures are compile/inspection expectations.
evidence: Make unexpansion of closure bodies more precise, by unexpanding back to the context of the closure declaration, instead of unexpanding all the way back to the top-level context.
Skip the normal span-refinement code when dealing with the trivial outer part of an async function.
Be more explicit about the fact that `fn_sig_span` has been extended to the start of the function body, and is not necessarily present.
This improves the coverage instrumentation of closures declared in macros
Only add the signature span if we found at least one span in the body.
